sentences.text: Huehuecanauhtlus was a medium-sized hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of western Mexico.
Researchers estimated this animal to be 6 meters long, 2.3 meters high, and weighing 1.5 tons.
The generic name Huehuecanauhtlus comes from Náhuatl words meaning "ancient" and "duck", pronounced "UEUE-CANA-UHh-TLUS".
Pathologies have been observed on the vertebrae and dorsal ribs of the holotype specimen, the specific individual the species is based on.
The animal is known only from two fossil individuals collected at the Barranca Los Bonetes locality in Tuzantla, Michoacán.
It was first described and named in 2012 by Angel Alejandro Ramírez-Velasco and colleagues, with the specific name tiquichensis honoring the town of Tiquicheo.
Excluding Claosaurus, Jeyawati, Levnesovia, Nanyangosaurus, Shuangmiaosaurus, and Telmatosaurus results in a more resolved phylogenetic topology for Huehuecanauhtlus.
Fossils date to the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 85.8 to 83.5 million years ago.
Reconstructions suggest Huehuecanauhtlus lived in the arid paramos that dominated the Cutzamala Formation.
